notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I don't have any notes for you yet. Every attempt to use the search and fetch tools was refused with a message saying I had no tool calls left for this turn. The block hit my very first request, so I didn't read a single source page.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read nothing, I can't write notes for any verse, and anything I wrote would come from memory with no URL behind it.

If you send the request again in a new turn, this is what I'll check:

1. **Verse-by-verse readings:** Enduring Word on Psalm 109; the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages on biblehub.com; Precept Austin; and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (on spurgeon.org or studylight.org).
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** mainly the curses in vv. 6–20. I'll look at how Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Lutheran and Pentecostal teachers deal with them. I'll also check where verses 6–19 are spoken by the psalmist's enemies rather than by David (both "him" and "my accusers" appear). Finally, I'll look at how Acts 1:20 applies v. 8 to Judas.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible translation notes on vv. 6–19; Bible Odyssey on psalms of cursing; and Augustine's sermon on this psalm on newadvent.org (in older Catholic Bibles it's numbered Psalm 108). I'll also check Catholic and Orthodox pages on how these curses are used in public worship. Popular modern teaching only goes in if one of the allowed sites actually covers it.

You can also paste in pages from those sites yourself, and I'll write the notes from them, with the URL after each point.
